instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Thinly slice the half onion. Cut the tofu into 1/2 inch cubes. Wash the mustard greens and cut them into 1 inch pieces. Grate the ginger and slice the green onions.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until soft and fragrant.
Add the salt and tamari and stir for 30 seconds. Add the broth, turn the heat to high and bring to a boil.
Add the tofu, ginger and sugar. Turn the heat to medium-low and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the mustard greens and simmer for 4 to 6 minutes, until they are tender and jade green. Check them early so they don't overcook.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the white pepper. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle into bowls, top with the green onions and serve with the rice.
method_notes: Viet World Kitchen's Canh Cai Dau Hu is the lead: onion softened in oil, water and a salty seasoning, then tofu and the mustard greens simmered until jade green. It has chicken and fish sauce, so for vegan and gluten-free both go and tamari replaces the fish sauce, as 328North suggests, with its ginger and pinch of sugar for the greens' bitterness. Gluten-free vegetable broth replaces water so the soup has body without the chicken. None of the three versions read had ratings, and RecipeTin Eats has no version.
